Norway's royal family gathers at King Harald's bedside as his condition worsens
- Published
King Harald V of Norway is in an "extremely serious" condition in hospital, the country's royal household has said.
His wife, Queen Sonja, and his son, Crown Prince Haakon, have cancelled all royal engagements and they have gathered at his bedside at Oslo University Hospital with other members of the royal family.
The 89-year-old has been in hospital for over a week receiving treatment for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia.
Having been on the throne since 1991, King Harald is Europe's oldest head of state.
Crown Prince Haakon, 53, the successor to the Norwegian throne, has been serving as regent while his father is on leave.
King Harald has been treated in recent weeks with cortisone for haemolytic anaemia, a condition that causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced, and leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
Members of the royal family were seen arriving at the hospital on Thursday morning, including Haakon's wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit and her son Marius Borg Høiby.
King Harald's sister, Princess Astrid is also at the hospital, according to reports in Norwegian media.
Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre has cancelled a planned trip to Germany, where he was expected to meet Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday.
"The whole nation is with us as we send warm thoughts to the king and the rest of the royal family," he said in a statement.
Members of the public have also begun laying flowers in Palace Square, in front of the palace in Oslo.
The king has had multiple health problems in recent years which have forced him to scale back his royal duties.
He was fitted with a pacemaker in 2024 after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.
The Norwegian royal family has already faced a challenging year in 2026.
Crown Princess Mette-Marit received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.
The transplant came two days after Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges and is to appeal the sentence.
Høiby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.
Also earlier in the year, documents were released revealing Mette-Marit's frequent contact with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
She later apologised to Norway's king and queen for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.

Malaysia’s former PM Ismail Sabri charged with concealing assets
Ismail Sabri, 66, pleaded not guilty to a charge that allege he failed to provide a complete declaration of assets.
Former Malaysian Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob has been charged with failing to declare tens of millions of dollars worth of assets, becoming the country’s third former prime minister to face criminal charges after leaving office.
The 66-year-old pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court on Thursday to a charge that alleges he failed to provide a complete declaration of assets to Malaysia’s anti-corruption agency.

He is accused of concealing holdings worth about $40m, spread across nine currencies, as well as bars of gold and silver.

Russia’s 4th-Largest Oil Refinery Halts Processing After Drone Strike
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:56:28 UTC
17:56:28 KST

LUKOIL-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez, Russia’s fourth-largest oil refinery by capacity and its second-largest gasoline producer, has stopped processing crude oil following a Ukrainian drone strike.
Three industry sources told Reuters that the attack damaged several processing units, equipment connecting the units, and other refinery facilities.
The sources could not say how long it would take to repair the damage and resume oil refining at the plant.
The refinery, located in the city of Kstovo in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region, was hit in the early hours of August 26.
Video recorded by local residents showed several fires burning at the facility.
After previous attacks, LUKOIL-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez had already suspended operations because of damage to its processing equipment. One of the attacks took place on July 2.
The Kstovo refinery has a maximum annual capacity of about 17 million tonnes of crude oil.
Before the Ukrainian strikes, the refinery could produce around 5 million tonnes of gasoline, more than 5 million tonnes of diesel, 2 million tonnes of fuel oil, and about 500,000 tonnes of bitumen each year. Overall, the refinery produced more than 50 types of petroleum products.
Following a Ukrainian strike on August 21, LUKOIL-Permnefteorgsintez, Russia’s seventh-largest refinery by oil-processing capacity, suspended operations at its plant in the city of Perm.
The drone attack caused a fire and damaged processing equipment at the AVT-4 crude oil distillation unit, which accounts for nearly 40% of the refinery’s total capacity. Before the damage, the unit could process 14,000 metric tonnes of crude oil per day.
Another crude oil distillation unit, AVT-5, which accounts for 34% of the refinery’s total capacity, has remained offline since a drone attack on July 29.

Taiwan: Proposed judicial caning referendum indicates further erosion of human rights protection
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:54:36 UTC
17:54:36 KST

Ahead of the meeting of the Central Election Commission on 28 August regarding a proposed referendum on introducing judicial caning as a criminal punishment in Taiwan, Amnesty International Taiwan’s Director, E-Ling Chiu, said:
“It is both disturbing and disgraceful that the Legislative Yuan has chosen to advance a referendum proposal on judicial caning that clearly breaches international human rights law.
“This proposal is part of a broader pattern that has emerged in recent months. Human rights-related budgets have been cut, the work of independent institutions such as the National Human Rights Commission has been obstructed and the functioning of the Constitutional Court has been undermined. The advancement of a referendum seeking to legitimize cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment further contributes to the erosion of the human rights protection framework that Taiwan has spent decades building.”
Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director Sarah Brooks added:
“When public anger over crimes is exploited for political gain at the expense of human rights, everyone stands to lose.
“Amnesty International opposes any legislative proposal to introduce judicial caning in Taiwan and calls on the government to reaffirm its commitment to Article 7 of the ICCPR and the absolute prohibition of torture and other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment.”
Background
On 14 August 2026, Taiwan’s Legislative Yuan approved a referendum proposal asking voters whether the government should enact legislation introducing judicial caning as a special criminal punishment for offences including sexual assault, child abuse, high-value fraud and aggravated fraud. The proposal comes amid growing public anger over these offences fuelled by a series of highly publicized cases.
Shortly after the proposal was approved, Amnesty International Taiwan joined civil society organizations in issuing a joint statement expressing concern that judicial caning would violate human rights protections and contravene internationally recognized standards prohibiting corporal punishment.
The caning proposal is one of three referendum initiatives currently under consideration by Taiwan’s Central Election Commission. The Commission is scheduled to deliberate on the proposals on 28 August before deciding whether they may proceed to a nationwide vote. If the Central Election Commission approves, the referendum will be held in November 2026, alongside a national election.
The International Review Committee in May of this year confirmed that corporal punishment constitutes cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment in violation of the right to personal integrity and human dignity in Article 7 ICCPR. Amnesty International opposes corporal punishment in all circumstances and has consistently called on governments worldwide to abolish punishments such as caning, flogging, whipping and other forms of corporal punishment that are incompatible with the absolute prohibition of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

Hong Kong lowers heat stress warning system thresholds after calls for revamp
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:52:59 UTC
17:52:59 KST

Hong Kong lowers heat stress warning system thresholds after calls for revamp
Labour Department says updates include automatically raising alert level when temperatures in multiple parts of the city reach 35 degrees Celsius
Hong Kong labour authorities have unveiled changes to the system that sends out warnings to workers about overexertion during very hot weather, reducing thresholds so higher-tier alerts can be issued more easily following intense criticism of the mechanism.
The Labour Department said on Thursday that two new conditions would be introduced to the Heat Stress at Work Warning system from Friday.
The system has three warning levels – amber, red and black – which alert employers and staff to the severity of heat stress if they are working outdoors or indoors without air conditioning.
The first change will reduce the threshold for triggering a higher-tier warning if the Observatory has already issued the extremely hot weather special alert, to ensure a quicker response.
The second change will see the warning automatically be raised by one level – from amber to red, or from red to black – when the measured temperatures generally over Hong Kong reach 35 degrees Celsius (95 Fahrenheit) or above.
The revamp was introduced after the system faced criticism over the lack of higher alerts earlier this month, when the city was grappling with record-breaking temperatures.

Fan backlash as gay World Cup star joins Saudi club
- Published
Spain forward Esther Gonzalez has attracted backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.
The 33-year-old agreed a mutual contract termination with National Women's Soccer League champions Gotham FC in July to temporarily step away from the sport to "attend to personal matters in Spain", according to the club's statement.
Gonzalez, whose contract was due to expire in 2027, said on Instagram the decision was "due to strictly personal reasons", adding New York-based Gotham will "always hold a special place in my heart".
However, on Sunday, Al Qadsiah announced the signing of the 2023 World Cup winner, sparking criticism from both Gotham fans over the nature of her departure, and from within the LGBTQ+ community.
Same-sex relationships and sexual activity are illegal in Saudi Arabia.
Fans on social media questioned her motivations and expressed concerns for her safety while Gotham supporters voiced their disappointment over the messaging around her exit and the club missing out on a transfer fee.
According to Spanish outlet El Mundo,, external Gonzalez has deleted all photos of herself with her wife and their first child, born in January, from her social media accounts since signing for Al Qadsiah.
Gonzalez is not the first footballer to encounter negative reactions for moving to Saudi Arabia, with England midfielder Jordan Henderson attracting criticism following his transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq in 2023.
The move was described as a "slap in the face" by openly gay footballer Jake Daniels, who had received a message of support from Henderson when he came out.
The former Liverpool captain, who had previously shown his support for the LGBTQ+ community by wearing rainbow laces, a One Love armband, and writing messages of solidarity in a matchday programme, left Al-Ettifaq after six months.
Gonzalez won two NWSL titles, an NWSL Challenge Cup, and the Concacaf W Champions Cup in three seasons after moving to the United States from Real Madrid.
Al Qadsiah finished fourth in the Saudi Women's Premier League in 2025-26.
Gotham FC declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

Nearly 900 foreign tourists remained missing Thursday in Nepal and China’s Tibet region following devastating flash floods and landslides that killed at least 180 people, official figures showed.
According to the Nepal Tourism Board, 644 foreign and local tourists are missing on the Nepalese side of the border.
They include 178 from India, 65 from the US, 53 from Ukraine, 51 from Malaysia, 35 from Australia, 33 from the UK, 25 from Canada, nine from Singapore and eight from Germany.
Other missing tourists are from France, Hungary, Switzerland, Italy, Ireland, Israel, Japan, Kazakhstan, Portugal, Russia and other countries.
An additional 127 Nepalese tourists are also unaccounted for, the board said.
China’s Foreign Ministry said 100 Chinese nationals were missing on the Nepalese side of the border due to the flash floods.
Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said 260 foreign nationals remained unaccounted for in Tibet, which Beijing identifies as the Xizang Autonomous Region.
Figures provided by the Nepalese government did not include the missing Chinese nationals.
The floods were likely triggered by a large chunk of ice breaking off a Himalayan glacier about 20 kilometers (12.4 miles) northeast of the Rasuwa-Rasuwagadhi border crossing, according to satellite imagery.
Nepalese authorities confirmed 177 deaths and recorded 826 people missing.
Chinese authorities said three people were killed and 558 remained missing, including foreign nationals.

Ukrposhta has established an aviation security service to inspect international parcels
Kyiv • UNN
Ukrposhta has established an aviation security service to detect dangerous contents before shipments are sent abroad. It serves 159 routes to 230 countries.
Ukrposhta has created its own aviation security service, which checks international shipments while they are still in Ukraine. This was reported by the Ministry for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine, according to UNN.
Details
Faster and safer delivery of Ukrainian parcels worldwide. Ukrposhta has created its own aviation security service. Its task is to identify dangerous and prohibited contents while they are still in Ukraine, as they could cause an entire batch of international shipments to be delayed
In particular, according to the ministry, one problematic parcel can lead to additional inspections of hundreds of other shipments. For Ukrainian businesses, such delays can affect delivery times, customer trust, marketplace ratings, and the ability to compete abroad.
Today, Ukrposhta uses 159 air routes and exchanges mail with 230 countries and territories around the world. Specialists use modern X-ray systems to inspect shipments. The service is being developed in cooperation with the State Customs Service and UNODC, whose experts have already conducted specialized training for Ukrposhta employees. The next step is to install more X-ray systems at automated sorting hubs. Fewer risks and unnecessary inspections mean a faster route for Ukrainian goods to buyers worldwide
We would like to remind you
The government explained the customs bill for reforming the taxation of international parcels, which was approved yesterday and submitted to parliament for consideration.

Unknown Publisher

ALBAWABA - Alleged mastermind of the 9/11 attacks is set to stand trial in June of 2028 – 25 years later.
Khalid Sheikh Mohammad, self-proclaimed "mastermind" of the 9/11 attacks, has been held in the U.S. Guantanamo Bay detention center since 2006 following his capture three years earlier; he is now set to stand trial on Monday, 5 June 2028, according to U.S. Lt. Col. Michael Schrama.
The court date comes after a controversial turn of events in 2024, where Khalid, along with two other defendants, were offered a plea agreement by military prosecutors.
The deal stated they had to plead guilty to 9/11 including the 3,000 people killed in the attack, in return, the court promised it would cancel the death penalty with the defendants serving a life sentence at Guantanamo, instead.
This decision proved to be highly controversial amongst the American public, especially those whose family members were victims of the terrorist attack.
The criticism was severe enough for then-Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin to revoke the deal, saying:
"I have determined that, in light of the significance of the decision to enter into pre-trial agreements with the accused in the above-referenced case, responsibility for such a decision should rest with me as the superior convening authority under the Military Commissions Act of 2009," Austin wrote.
Taking the plea off the table, it is highly probable that the defendants will be facing the death penalty at their trial in 2028.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The legislature decided Thursday to postpone consideration of referendum reforms that would allow multiple referendum questions to appear on a single ballot.
The KMT and TPP legislative caucuses had been poised to pass the referendum reform and drone legislation on the final day of the current legislative session. During caucus negotiations chaired by Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜), the KMT backed down and agreed to postpone the referendum reform, per ETtoday.
KMT Caucus Convener Fu Kun-chi (傅崐萁) said the party had received a request from Central Election Commission Chair You Ying-lung (游盈隆) and would strive to accommodate it, per SETN. He noted that the reforms would not take effect in the 2026 local elections, giving the CEC time to adapt and prepare.
You strongly objected to the opposition’s referendum reform proposal Wednesday, warning that rushed implementation could increase the risk of election-administration errors. He stressed that introducing changes less than 100 days before an election could create more problems than they solve.
The parties’ positions on the reform proposal largely fell along partisan lines. Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) cautioned against the proposal, noting its potential impact on voting and vote counting, per Tai Sounds. DPP legislative caucus official Fan Yun (范雲) echoed Cho’s warning, stressing that “elections could not be treated like experiments,” per Liberty Times.
Among opposition lawmakers, You’s comments drew pushback. KMT lawmaker Lai Shyh-pao (賴士葆) said the proposal was intended to avoid the chaos experienced during the 2018 local elections, when a large number of referendum questions significantly increased voting and vote-counting times, per UDN. He suggested that You’s criticism of the opposition’s reform proposal, without providing a workable alternative, was an attempt to reduce the number of referendum proposals.
TPP Legislative Caucus Convener Chen Ching-lung (陳清龍) rejected You’s characterization of the reform proposal as a “bad idea,” noting that the TPP’s version of the amendment would give the CEC greater flexibility, per FTNN. He argued that You had deliberately disregarded the TPP’s goodwill.

Allring Senior Vice President Chiang Cheng-yen (蔣正彥) said the firm must respond quickly to customer needs. He added that Allring chose Taichung because its main customers and partners are in central Taiwan, which shortens delivery, installation, and servicing times.
Allring said demand for advanced packaging and chip-cooling technology has grown alongside high-performance computing. It said it will focus on heat-dissipation technologies and equipment, including the use of highly thermally conductive materials in chip manufacturing processes. The firm added that it is also hiring to meet its growing operational needs.

Taiwan signs NT$26.9 billion deal for more than 2,000 Altius drones
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:45:25 UTC
17:45:25 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan has signed an NT$26.9 billion (US$847 million) contract to acquire more than 2,000 US-made attack and reconnaissance drones as it expands its asymmetric capabilities.
The Ministry of National Defense announced the contract Thursday through the government’s electronic procurement system. It covers 1,554 Altius-700M loitering munitions and 478 Altius-600ISR reconnaissance drones, per Liberty Times. The systems are manufactured by US defense technology company Anduril Industries and are expected to be deployed primarily with Army units.
The contract covers the drones, associated systems, and launch equipment, while the overall US arms package, previously announced at about NT$34.9 billion, includes additional components. The signing of the Letter of Offer and Acceptance formalizes the purchase.
The Army previously acquired 291 basic Altius-600M drones through its regular budget, with the systems reportedly achieving a 100% hit rate in a recent live-fire maritime exercise, Liberty Times reported. The performance helped support plans to significantly expand the drone fleet through the special budget.
The Altius-700M is designed to strike targets such as heavy armored vehicles and air defense systems, per China Times. It can carry a 14- to 15-kilogram heavy warhead capable of destroying modern main battle tanks or fortified positions, with destructive power nearly equivalent to that of an AGM-114 Hellfire missile.
The Altius-600ISR is an unmanned aerial vehicle designed for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions, including battlefield searches, target designation, and electronic warfare. With the same endurance as the Altius-600M, it can loiter over target areas for extended periods to conduct surveillance and support coordinated operations.
Initial deliveries of the new drones are expected to begin in the fourth quarter, with the full order scheduled for completion by June 2033, according to Liberty Times. The Ministry of National Defense said the acquisition will strengthen Taiwan’s defense resilience, while the Army has established a dedicated unit to develop unmanned systems and integrate them into its joint command structure.

Kuai Kuai is a popular Taiwanese snack often placed near computers and other machines as a symbol of good luck. Green packages are believed to help equipment run smoothly and prevent problems.

Taiwan consumer confidence edges up in August
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:44:58 UTC
17:44:58 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan’s consumer confidence index edged up in August, but the gauge for stock investment opportunities posted its biggest decline among the six sub-indexes, a National Central University survey showed Thursday.
The CCI rose 0.43 points from July to 65.01, while four sub-indexes increased and two fell, per UDN. None of the changes were statistically significant, suggesting overall consumer confidence was largely unchanged.
The job opportunities index posted the largest increase, rising 1.13 points as the impact of the annual graduation season faded. The price-level index also rose 0.75 point, although the survey was conducted before recent heavy rains in southern Taiwan had a clear impact on fruit and vegetable prices.
The stock investment opportunities index fell 0.36 point, the largest decline among the six measures. Taiwan Economic Development Director Wu Ta-jen (吳大任) said recent volatility in Taiwan stocks may have prompted investors to take a wait-and-see approach, per CNA.
Taiwan stocks fell below 40,000 points at the end of July before recovering somewhat in August, but the stronger performance in recent days was not reflected in the survey conducted Aug. 18-21. Wu said the decline in the index does not necessarily mean people have lost confidence in stocks, as some may consider prices relatively high and wait for a pullback before investing.
Wu said the sharp upward revision of Taiwan’s economic growth forecast this year to 11.05% by the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting, and Statistics on Aug. 14 likely had limited influence on the survey, as consumers tend to assess the economy based on their daily experiences. He said stock market performance can also shape perceptions of economic conditions, with rising markets making people feel more optimistic.
All six CCI sub-indexes remained below 100, indicating a pessimistic outlook. Wu explained that US economic conditions, Federal Reserve policy, AI infrastructure investment, and developments in the US-Iran situation will remain key factors affecting Taiwan’s economic and market outlook.

Royal Navy warship to provide air defence for Ireland
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
09:41:27 BST
17:41:27 KST

According to a report in The Irish Times, a Royal Navy warship will provide air defence during a meeting of EU defence and foreign affairs ministers in County Wicklow next week, while remaining outside Irish territorial waters because of constitutional restrictions.
A Royal Navy air defence warship is reportedly due to deploy to the Irish Sea next week at Ireland’s request to provide protection during a meeting of European Union defence and foreign affairs ministers in County Wicklow, according to The Irish Times.
Next week, at Ireland’s request, a Royal Navy warship will provide air defence during a meeting of EU ministers in Wicklow. But, to comply with the Irish Constitution, the ship must remain outside Irish territorial watershttps://t.co/54jJ8NNzxx
— Conor Gallagher (@ConorGallaghe_r) August 27, 2026
The unusual arrangement was reported by Irish Times investigations reporter Conor Gallagher, who said British and French warships providing air defence during Ireland’s six-month EU presidency have been required to remain around 22 kilometres offshore because of legal advice received by the Irish Government. Although Dublin formally requested assistance from the two navies, the report says officials were advised that foreign military forces conducting active operations inside Irish territory would likely raise constitutional problems.
Gallagher summarised the forthcoming British deployment on X, writing: “Next week, at Ireland’s request, a Royal Navy warship will provide air defence during a meeting of EU ministers in Wicklow. But, to comply with the Irish Constitution, the ship must remain outside Irish territorial waters.”
According to The Irish Times, advice from Ireland’s Attorney General concluded that the deployment of foreign military forces on active operations within Irish territory would likely be unconstitutional even where their presence had been formally requested by the Irish Government. The report cites Article 15 of the Irish Constitution in explaining the legal advice, saying officials were told that only the Oireachtas has the right to raise a military force on Irish territory.
The result is an air-defence arrangement in which allied warships can reportedly provide missile cover for major events in Ireland while remaining outside the country’s territorial waters. The Royal Navy deployment planned for next week’s ministerial meeting follows an earlier French operation during the opening of Ireland’s EU presidency.
The Irish Times reports that the French frigate Aquitaine was stationed in Dublin Bay, just outside the 22-kilometre limit, on 1 July while dozens of European heads of government were visiting Ireland. The ship reportedly provided air defence while Irish military aircraft and naval vessels were also deployed to secure the area.
The report says a separate legal issue arose over whether a foreign warship positioned outside Irish territorial waters could take lethal action against an airborne threat over Ireland, such as a hostile drone or hijacked aircraft. Under Irish Defence Forces rules of engagement, known internally as COD 6, only Irish military officers can authorise the use of force in such circumstances, according to the newspaper.
As a workaround, an Irish naval officer was reportedly placed aboard the French ship as a liaison officer and given responsibility for providing final authorisation if lethal force was required. The Irish Times reports that this could have included authorising the use of long-range anti-aircraft missiles against an airborne threat.
European warships are reportedly expected to continue providing air defence during major events for the remainder of Ireland’s EU presidency. According to the report, next week’s meeting of EU defence and foreign affairs ministers in County Wicklow will be supported by a Royal Navy air defence warship operating in the Irish Sea.
The Irish Government has not publicly confirmed the French frigate’s earlier security role. The Irish Times reported that Ireland’s Department of Defence referred questions to An Garda Síochána, while a Garda spokeswoman said the force had no knowledge of Operation Fianna, the military security operation mounted for Ireland’s EU presidency.
The forthcoming British deployment would therefore continue an arrangement under which Ireland has reportedly sought allied naval air-defence support for major international gatherings while keeping the ships conducting those operations outside Irish territorial waters. No specific Royal Navy vessel has been identified in the report, however.

How is the flood of information drowning human intellect?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:41:14 UTC
17:41:14 KST

Topic: Contemporary Psychology, Technology, and the Culture of Reading 
  
 Introduction: The Paradox of the 21st Century: We live in the richest era in history in terms of access to data. With just a few touches on the screen, we have access to libraries, articles, and analyses from all over the world. But why, despite this unprecedented abundance of information, do we feel that human society is becoming more superficial, more bored, and more oblivious day by day?
 
 What was predicted by thinkers two or three decades ago has today become our tangible, everyday reality: the ruthless encroachment of data on the privacy of thought and thought. We live in the age of information bombardment; an age in which the boundary between “knowledge” and “noise” has disappeared.
 
 1. From intellectual nourishment to brain "self-eating": The human brain has an amazing and flexible structure. Reading and learning are the engines of activation and development of this vital organ. But unlike cloud memories and digital hard drives, the brain's deep processing capacity is not unlimited.
 
 When data inputs exceed the brain's tolerance threshold, a reverse and destructive cycle begins: the phenomenon of cognitive self-eating.
 
 At this stage, the brain not only loses the ability to analyze and organize new data, but also, due to the lack of opportunity for "memory consolidation", slowly forgets the deep archive of knowledge and fundamental concepts that it had previously stored. We read more, but we understand less and forget faster.
 
 Daily data flood ──> Unstable concentration ──> Inability to analyze ──> Analysis of mental archive (decline of wisdom)
 
 2. Entering the World of “Post-Literacy”: New global analytical reports show that this crisis is not regional or limited to a specific culture; it is a pervasive and transnational phenomenon. We are rapidly moving into what experts call the “post-literacy era.”
 
 
 What is true literacy? Literacy is not simply the ability to read words; it is the possession of systematic, coherent, contextual, and in-depth knowledge about a subject.
 
 
 What is post-literacy? A state in which active readers have given way to “passive consumers.” In this age, people consume a vast amount of headlines, short messages, social media posts, and instant information, but they have lost the ability to understand complex texts, analyze long arguments, and connect concepts.
 
 3. The decline of art and the rise of “shallow artists”: The impact of this information overload is not limited to memory or general literacy; literature and art are also major victims of this trend.
 
 As today’s audience becomes bored and preoccupied with receiving a quick dopamine hit from social media, their tastes change. This change in tastes creates a damaging feedback loop:
 
 The consumer audience loses the ability to appreciate deep, complex, and layered works.
 
 The market and algorithms push artists to produce “simplistic,” “marketable,” and “quick-to-consume” works.
 
 As a result, a new generation of creators is emerging: superficial, shallow, and possibly meaningless.
 
 Art, once a haven for deep thought and the nurturing of human wisdom, has itself become a product of the same noise factory.
 
 4. Solution: Renaissance of classic media and "digital abstinence": To escape this cognitive swamp, one cannot hope for algorithms or newer technologies; because the essence of modern technologies is designed based on capturing momentary attention and fragmenting human concentration.
 
 The antidote to this crisis is a conscious return to classical principles: escaping the rigidity of the screen: reducing the distance from smartphones and the non-stop Internet is the first step to recovering the attention span.
Taking refuge in paper media (books and newspapers): Reading on paper allows the brain to think linearly, patiently and deeply. Unlike social networks, books do not contain "notifications" and distracting links; books invite you to "silence of thought".
 
 Slow Reading: Instead of accumulating information at hand, returning to original texts and reading them repeatedly re-waters the roots of wisdom in the mind.
 
 Conclusion: A choice for the future of humanity: We stand at a civilizational crossroads: do we want to be beings with a huge accumulation of worthless data and fragmented minds, or patient humans with deep wisdom and coherent thought?
 
 Saving thought, art, and literacy in today's world is a revolutionary act. This revolution begins with closing a tab in the browser, putting away your mobile phone, and opening a real book. Wisdom does not grow in the noise of data; wisdom is born in silence and depth.
MNA

Greece reports 232 West Nile virus cases, 19 deaths
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:38:49 UTC
17:38:49 KST

Necva Taştan Sevinç
27 August 2026•Update: 27 August 2026
Greece has reported 232 locally acquired West Nile virus cases and 19 related deaths during the 2026 transmission season, health authorities said Thursday.
Seventy-five new cases were diagnosed in the week ending Aug. 26, marking a sharp rise in infections, according to the National Public Health Organization’s latest epidemiological surveillance report.
The outbreak is nearly three times larger than during the corresponding period last year, Greek daily Tovima reported.
Of the confirmed patients, 165 developed complications affecting the central nervous system, including encephalitis, meningitis or acute flaccid paralysis.
Another 67 experienced mild symptoms or showed no neurological complications.
All 19 people who died were over 65, with a median age of 85. The victims ranged in age from 66 to 92.
Eighty-nine patients remain hospitalized across the country.
Deputy Health Minister Marios Themistokleous said mathematical models suggest that 2026 could become a record year, potentially exceeding the severe 2018 outbreak, when Greece registered 317 cases and 59 deaths.
Health authorities expect the current wave to peak within the next one to two weeks, although new infections are likely to continue through at least the end of September.
Health Minister Adonis Georgiadis said “there is no reason to panic,” stressing that the healthcare system is not under pressure.
A significant share of infections has been detected in the Attica region, where municipalities have intensified mosquito-control measures.
Authorities in Pallini are using a digital risk map to monitor storm drains and installing special traps targeting female mosquitoes.
In Filothei-Psychiko, emergency nighttime spraying was conducted within a 300-meter (984-foot) radius of a confirmed case.
Health authorities urged residents, particularly older people, to continue taking precautions against mosquito bites throughout the fall.

‘Swept away’: Nepal families search for relatives after devastating floods
About 180 people have been killed and 1,400 are missing, with numbers expected to rise significantly after apparent glacial collapse in Tibet unleashes flash floods.
Kathmandu, Nepal — It was a normal school day on Wednesday at Trishuli Secondary School in Nepal’s Nuwakot district when Gyan Deep Sapkota, a grade 11 student, suddenly heard his teachers yelling.
Bidur, the city where the school is based, lies on the banks of the Trishuli river. A flash flood was barrelling down from upstream, where the river is known as the Bhotekoshi.
“Our teachers were shouting for us to leave,” he recalled, speaking to Al Jazeera on the phone. “Some of us took a small old bridge and crossed to a safer area, while most of the students took up to the hills. Some of the students also had panic attacks and fainted.
“It’s still giving me goosebumps and anxiety.”
About 180 people have been killed and at least 1,400 people are missing in a vast region spanning Nepal and Tibet in China, after a suspected glacial lake outburst upstream in Tibet caused a massive flash flood that swept away entire settlements and even dams in the way. Among the missing are police, government employees, hydropower engineers and Nepalese, apart from hundreds of foreign tourists in Nepal.
By late on Wednesday, Nepal Police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle said that search and rescue teams had recovered 95 bodies. But both the death toll and the number of missing are expected to rise significantly, as the water recedes and connectivity with the worst-hit regions is re-established. Senior superintendent Rajendra Prasad Dhamala, a police officer monitoring the search in the Bagmati province, one of the regions affected, said most of the bodies recovered were found in downstream areas.
Many of those missing are Indian tourists who were heading to Tibet for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, a major Hindu pilgrimage to a lake that is sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Jains.
‘Everything has been swept away’
Healthcare worker Rajendra Poudel, a resident of Betrawati, a town in Nuwakot district, described apocalyptic scenes.
“Till early this morning it was very scenic around here. There were houses and horticulture gardens here. There was a hydropower station and plant. Everything has been swept away,” Poudel told Al Jazeera.
“There is nothing here. This is heartbreaking; I am out of words.”
Lal Bahadur Rai, another resident of Nuwakot district, said the floodwaters reached within 10 metres of his house. “Many houses and even a school across the banks of my village have been swept away. My house was just lucky,” he said.
“There were solar power stations in the area, all of which have been wiped. There is also huge coffee farming here. All of it is gone now.”
A statement released by Nepal’s Prime Minister’s Office said 19 vehicle bridges and 43km of highway connecting lower regions of the Himalayan nation to the affected areas have been swept away by the flood.
The Nepali districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan have been kept under high alert, while authorities have urged citizens to stay far away from the rivers.
Prime Minister Balen Shah, in a social media post, called for “national unity” during the crisis and urged local groups, businesses, young volunteers and citizens across the country to contribute from wherever they are and support the government’s relief and rescue campaign.
“The search for citizens missing in the floods will be intensified further,” posted Shah. India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi also spoke to Shah on Wednesday and assured humanitarian assistance and support.
Searching for missing relatives
That search has seen resident Rajan Nepali visit numerous hospitals in the capital, Kathmandu, where some of those rescued were airlifted.
“My brother-in-law was accompanying tourists in Rasuwa [district]. He was in touch with us till 8am in the morning. After that, his phone has been switched off and he has been out of touch,” Nepali told Al Jazeera from the National Trauma Center in Kathmandu. “We have been looking for him in hospitals. We do not know where to go, what to do.”
Janak Raj Bohora, a civil engineer working with the Upper Trishuli hydropower project for the last four years, has been missing since the floods.
“I talked to him on Wednesday morning at 6am, but haven’t been in touch after he went for his duty. I have no information on where he is till now,” his wife, Sharmila Bhandari, told Al Jazeera, from Bajhang in western Nepal.
Dipesh Dhakal, who was working for the same hydropower project, has also been missing since the floods. Bishnu Adhikari, Dhakal’s friend, said that many in his team had successfully fled after a siren alarm went off.
But it is unclear if Dhakal made it out of the flood’s path in time. “Since the phones are not working, we cannot say,” he said.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Ozon Logistics Hubs in Russia as Marketplace Warehouses Come Under Sustained Attack
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:35:22 UTC
17:35:22 KST

Ukrainian drones struck Ozon logistics facilities in Ufa and Orenburg overnight on Wednesday, Aug. 27, the Russian online marketplace said, as attacks on Russia’s major e-commerce infrastructure continue to disrupt warehouses across the country.
Ozon said it evacuated all employees from the affected sites and that there were no casualties or fires.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The Ufa warehouse sustained “minor damage” and has been temporarily closed, with deliveries from sellers suspended. The Orenburg distribution center has resumed operations but will not accept some goods during the day, according to the company.
The strikes follow a wave of attacks targeting Russia’s biggest online marketplaces.
Since mid-July, more than 20 Wildberries distribution centers across 16 Russian regions have come under Ukrainian drone attack. At least seven of the company’s 10 largest warehouses have reportedly been knocked out of operation, including its main facility in Koledino, Moscow Oblast.
Ozon has also increasingly become a target. Attacks began on Aug. 22 with a strike on a facility in Chapayevsk in Russia’s Samara region, followed the next day by an attack in Orenburg.
On Aug. 24, four Ozon warehouses in Makhachkala, Krasnodar, Adygea, and Nevinnomyssk were hit in a single night. Fires were reported at all four sites.
The strikes have inflicted potentially hundreds of billions of rubles in losses on Russia’s e-commerce sector.
How Russia Finds the Cracks in American Society – and Widens Them
Ukraine inflicts heavy damage to Wildberries
Analysts at Data Insight estimated Wildberries’ losses from destroyed warehouse inventory at 147–223 billion rubles ($1.8-2.8 billion), while sellers could have lost another 445-507 billion rubles ($5.5-6.3 billion). Total losses could reach 800 billion rubles ($10 billion).
Ozon’s potential losses have been estimated at 30-62.5 billion rubles ($375-781 million), with sellers facing an additional 88.5-107 billion rubles ($1.1-1.3 billion) in losses.
According to the same Data Insight estimate, Wildberries has lost around one-third of its warehouse space following repeated Ukrainian drone strikes.
“Wildberries has almost run out of its biggest warehouses,” Data Insight analyst Sergei Semko told The New York Times.
Separately, Reuters reported that at least 1.18 million square meters (292 acres) of Wildberries warehouse space had been damaged or destroyed. That amounts to more than one-fifth of its total capacity.
One Moscow-based source told Reuters that his deliveries had fallen from around 400 parcels a day to about 150, adding that he was trying to sell his business.
Ukraine has described Wildberries as a legitimate target due to them selling products with possible military use, such as first-person-view (FPV) drones and fiber-optic cables.
Wildberries, however, denied supplying Russia’s armed forces, saying weapons and military equipment are prohibited from sale on its marketplace.
The company accounts for around 10% of Russian retail sales, making it a significant contributor to Russia’s wartime economy.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has sought to downplay the impact, saying Ukrainian drone attacks had caused Russia no “critical consequences.”
Yet Putin also signed a decree allowing the Russian state to place businesses and facilities under temporary state control if their owners fail to protect them from drone strikes.
The Kremlin said the measure was needed because businesses were not doing enough to protect strategically important facilities from attacks.

Tanzania's ruling party picks new candidate for vice president
DAR ES SALAAM, Aug 27 - Tanzania's ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi party has picked the energy minister as its nominee for the new vice president, the party's secretary general said late on Wednesday, after the incumbent announced his resignation less than a year into the job.
Outgoing Vice President Emmanuel John Nchimbi will leave office on September 4, having served since last November. His resignation followed criticism from some in the party for remarks about the constitution last month that they considered unnecessary.
The ruling party's National Executive Committee has now picked Deogratius Ndejembi for nomination as the next vice president, ruling party secretary general Asha-Rose Migiro told reporters.
NEC "has unanimously approved that member to take the position of Vice President. This will take place after completing the constitutional procedures that require his name to be submitted to Parliament," Migiro said.
Ndejembi would be sworn in after he has been approved by parliament, she added.
She said the ruling party had also decided to expel Nchimbi from the party "due to conduct that violated our regulations regarding discipline and ethics". She did not say what conduct violated the party's rules.
Last month Nchimbi urged Tanzanians to fight for a new constitution, "a constitution that leads us toward development, not just material and economic development, but the development of dignity and the human worth of every person living in Tanzania," he said.
President Samia Suluhu Hassan won last year's presidential election with nearly 98% of the vote, in an election marred by deadly violence. REUTERS

Three Russians of Chechen origin detained in Warsaw, three firearms seized
The Polish police and Poland's Internal Security Agency have detained three Russian nationals of Chechen origin in Warsaw. A search of a flat in the Wola district has uncovered three firearms and ammunition.
Source: European Pravda, citing Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński on X (Twitter)
Quote from Kierwiński: "Three Russian nationals of Chechen origin have been detained. Illegal firearms and ammunition were found in a flat in Warsaw's Wola district."
Details: Police seized three firearms during the search, Onet reported. The detainees are men aged 21, 25 and 42.
At the request of the Warsaw-Wola District Prosecutor's Office, the 42-year-old man has been remanded in custody for three months. He faces between six months and eight years in prison.
Deportation proceedings have been launched against the 25-year-old man. The 21-year-old was released after being questioned as a witness.
The arrests took place last weekend after the security services received information about possible activities by an organised crime group.
Background:
- On 15 June 2026, Russian artist Semyon Skrepetsky, who was known for being critical of Vladimir Putin, was killed in the Polish city of Biała Podlaska in the Lublin Voivodeship. A gunman approached him and fired twice. When Skrepetsky fell to the ground, the killer went over to him and fired three more shots at close range.
- Russian opposition activist Sergei Vlasenko was recently found dead in a flat in Warsaw. The post-mortem found no injuries suggesting the involvement of third parties.
- Polish authorities previously detained a Russian national suspected of plotting to kill a Ukrainian-US citizen.

More than 86,000 children have been born in Kyiv during the full-scale war
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
11:31:11 EEST
17:31:11 KST

More than 86,000 children have been born in Kyiv during the full-scale war
Kyiv • UNN
Since the start of the invasion, 86,526 children have been born in Kyiv’s municipal medical facilities. Among them were 1,468 sets of twins and 14 sets of triplets.
In the period since the start of the full-scale invasion, more than 86,500 babies have been born in the capital. The Kyiv City State Administration’s Department of Health released these figures, UNN reports.
The Kyiv City State Administration’s Department of Health also reported that, since the beginning of the full-scale war and as of August 20, 2026, 86,526 children had been born at the capital’s municipal healthcare facilities. Among them were 44,579 boys and 41,947 girls. This included 1,468 sets of twins and 14 sets of triplets.
Such deliveries often take place in shelters. For example, as reported by the capital’s Perinatal Center, on the night of August 27, four deliveries were handled in the shelters of two of the center’s branches.
"Every child born in Kyiv during the full-scale war is a symbol of Ukrainians’ faith in victory and their resilience. Our medical professionals have learned to work in extremely challenging conditions. Today, all municipal maternity hospitals and perinatal centers have the necessary equipment to provide assistance in critical situations. Even during the longest air-raid alerts, we continue to do everything possible to protect the lives and health of mothers and their children," emphasized Tetiana Mostepan, Director of the Kyiv City Department of Health.
How the shelters at the capital’s Perinatal Center are equipped
UNN has already reported on how the shelters at the capital’s Perinatal Center are equipped and how they operate. Shelters are available at both branches. They were equipped with the assistance of UNICEF and Procter & Gamble.
As Perinatal Center Director Dmytro Hovsieiev explained, the bomb shelters include delivery rooms and operating rooms equipped with ventilators and oxygenators.
They also have the necessary equipment for caring for premature and newborn infants, as well as beds for patients and wards for the second stage of infants’ care. There is also an area accessible to visitors to the Center who need to wait out an air-raid alert.
Born in a shelter: how the maternity hospital's bomb shelter operates30.06.26, 17:32 • 21889 views
The bomb shelters are designed for prolonged stays. The shelters have separate generators, supplies of technical water in concrete reservoirs, as well as stocks of drinking water and some food products (tea, sugar, freeze-dried soups, and porridge).
In recent months, the capital has experienced air-raid alerts almost every night, and during them staff and patients go down to the shelter. The Perinatal Center has an established protocol, and every employee on duty knows their role.
The entire medical team is ready to act in accordance with approved emergency response algorithms—without interruptions or panic. Evacuation routes have been developed for critical situations, and communication with city services is maintained continuously.
As the center’s doctors told UNN , unfortunately, deliveries in shelters have already become routine, but the most important thing is the safety of the mother and the newborn.

Nepal and China step up rescue efforts day after catastrophic flood (VIDEOS)
Nepal has ramped up rescue efforts as it searches for thousands of people missing along its northern border with China, where a catastrophic flash flood wiped out towns and villages on Wednesday morning, killing more than 330 people.
Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said Thursday that thousands of families have lost their homes and remain untraced.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority in Nepal said 826 people are missing, with the Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts being the worst affected. The authority said 44 Nepalese Army personnel, 28 police personnel, and 13 Armed Police Force personnel are among those missing.
The Nepalese Army and private helicopters are conducting rescue missions, with about a 100 people rescued from the affected areas, spokesperson Brigadier General Raja Ram Basnet said. Army teams also rescued people trapped in the Trishuli hydropower project’s facilities.
At least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to Kathmandu by the army, he said.
Videos posted online by the army show its personnel rescuing people trapped in the thick, concrete-like mud covering many of the villages and towns that stood in the flood’s path.

“Rehabilitation is the major concern” for the Nepalese government as people have lost their homes, the spokesman for the Nepalese Prime Minister’s Office, Hemraj Aryal, told RT India. “The main thing is revitalizing and re-engaging the people in the society.”
He said rescue teams are already on most sites where people need help, but added that reconnecting the roads will take time as the devastation is huge.
China, where 558 people are missing in Tibet, dispatched 111 emergency rescuers to Gyirong Port in Xizang carrying detection, life-saving, demolition, communication, and support equipment. With roads washed away or damaged, the team was flown from Chengdu early Thursday morning, landing at Dingri Airport in Shigatse.

Zhipu AI shares jump as viral Ox Alpha model revealed as GLM-5.3-Flash on Chinese chips
Model shows China can scale AI on domestic chips, setting a usage record as Beijing pushes to cut reliance on US hardware
2-MIN READ2-MIN

Minxiao Changin Shenzhen
China’s Zhipu AI has launched its latest open-weight model, GLM-5.3-Flash – previously code-named Ox Alpha – saying that the system ran entirely on a cluster of 100,000 domestically produced chips during a high-profile stealth trial.
The announcement followed a week of heavy traffic on artificial intelligence model marketplace OpenRouter and agent platform OpenCode, where the model processed 62 trillion tokens before its formal release on Wednesday, according to Zhipu.
On OpenRouter, the system processed more than 11 trillion tokens in its first three days, making it the platform’s biggest launch to date.
Zhipu’s shares closed more than 12 per cent higher at HK$1,160 in Hong Kong on Thursday.
The deployment marks a significant test of China’s ability to handle large-scale global inference workloads on home-grown hardware, as Beijing seeks to reduce reliance on advanced processors from US market leader Nvidia amid tight export controls.
During its preview, Ox Alpha rapidly surged to the top of global usage rankings. According to OpenRouter data on Thursday, the model ranked first among coding systems on the platform, accounting for 10.3 trillion tokens, or nearly 31 per cent of its total weekly volume.

How Shenzhen can win the ‘AI for science’ race
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:30:10 UTC
17:30:10 KST

How Shenzhen can win the ‘AI for science’ race
Rather than copy the research-focused models of Beijing and Shanghai, the tech hub must leverage its industrial depths to become a premier lab for experimentation and deployment
The opportunity is obvious: AI could become a new source of scientific productivity and industrial growth. The trap is copying what other cities are doing. Shenzhen should not try to become Beijing with more hardware, or Shanghai with a different set of industry labels; it should build around its own comparative advantage.
The first advantage is the structure of its innovation economy. Shenzhen invested 245.31 billion yuan in research and development in 2024, the highest R&D intensity among Chinese cities. Strikingly, companies accounted for over 93 per cent of that spending. Those figures describe a city where research, engineering and commercial deployment sit unusually close together. This matters in the AI-for-science drive because the hard part isn’t only inventing an algorithm, but turning it into a reliable scientific tool.

CDU's Volkmann: Ukraine aid is not charity
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:30:00 UTC
17:30:00 KST

CDU's Volkmann: Ukraine aid is not charity
August 27, 2026
At 29, Johannes Volkmann is one of the youngest members of Germany's parliament — and one of the most dedicated supporters of Ukraine. When he was head of the council of the Lahn-Dill district in the state of Hessen, he launched a municipal partnership with the Ukrainian city of Brovary near the capital Kyiv to deliver supplies to those in need.
As a member of the Bundestag's Committee on Foreign Affairs and the United4Ukraine group, an international network of lawmakers, he continues to advocate for Ukraine. During his latest trip to the country, he spoke with DW about why he thinks aid to Ukraine is so important.
DW: Mr. Volkmann, you were last in Ukraine exactly a year ago. What has changed since then?
Johannes Volkmann: The number of airstrikes — and thus the threat to the civilian population — has increased significantly again. And at the same time, there is a sense that the Ukrainian people still want to stand their ground. I have utmost respect for that. Ukraine is demonstrating that freedom and democracy can defend themselves and fight back. That is a very important message of hope.
German support is particularly important for Ukraine's defense capabilities — Germany is the largest bilateral donor to Ukraine in Europe. At the same time, political forces in Germany oppose this support. The voters of these parties share this view and consider aid to Ukraine a waste of money. What would you say to them?
Everyone needs to understand that Ukraine today is not only defending itself, but also protecting Europe. Russian imperialism is not only a threat to Ukraine's borders, but also to those of our allies in the Baltic states and in Poland. That is why every euro we invest in Ukraine today is a good investment in our own security.
On top of that, Ukraine is able to help us more and more in Europe by sharing its experience on the battlefield with European armies — with regard to modern technologies, drones, the training of soldiers and modern tactics.
When it comes to experience, Ukraine has a tremendous lead in these areas. That is why Ukraine is now effectively a provider of security in Europe and no longer merely in need of security.
The Alternative for Germany (AfD), which currently leads the polls, has called for an end to German support for Ukraine. Many in Ukraine are wondering: What will happen if the AfD performs even better in the next German election and becomes part of the government?
I can understand this fear. The Bundestag was elected to serve until 2029. For me personally, as well as for my parliamentary group, the CDU/CSU, it is clear that Ukraine must be supported militarily because it is in our own interest in terms of security. For me, the AfD's position on Ukraine is an important reason why my party has ruled out any cooperation with them.
There is also a humanitarian responsibility: If millions of Ukrainians flee their homeland because Russia's war of aggression succeeds — and, of course, they won't want to live under Russian colonial rule — then that will destabilize our countries. That would place a much greater financial burden on us than supporting Ukrainians today in their defense of their homeland.
Do you view Russia as a military threat to Europe and Germany? Some are asking: If Russia has struggled so much in Ukraine militarily, what threat can it pose to NATO?
It is important to understand that Russia's hybrid attacks on Europe are not primarily aimed at military conquest but rather at achieving certain political objectives. These include the destruction of EU and NATO cohesion.
So, it is entirely possible that Russia, perhaps with threats involving nuclear weapons, could attempt to occupy specific areas in the Baltic region to test the significance of NATO's Article 5 — the solidarity clause. This is why it is all the more important that we remain vigilant about this issue and develop the capacity to defend ourselves in order to deter Russia from any such aggression. We can only protect peace through our own strength; weakness will be seen as an invitation to attack.
Germany was one of the countries particularly hesitant and cautious regarding Ukraine's possible accession to NATO. At the 2008 NATO summit in the Romanian capital Bucharest, it was against granting Ukraine a Membership Action Plan (MAP). Many in Ukraine believe that their country's rapid admission into NATO — or at least the granting of an MAP — could have prevented Russia's hybrid war in 2014 and the full-scale invasion in 2022. Was Germany's policy at the time a mistake?
It is clear that the hypothesis put forward by the German government at the time has turned out to have been wrong — the assumption that trade, for example in gas via the Nord Stream pipeline, would create mutual dependencies and thus prevent violence from occurring. The same applies to the assumption that neutrality would protect other countries.
It was a big mistake for Germany to not listen to the insights of our neighbors to the east, who, because of their own experiences with Moscow, historically have a much better understanding of what Russia actually wants.
Apart from accession to NATO, many Ukrainians view membership of the European Union as the best guarantee of security. But German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has ruled out Ukraine's accelerated admission to the bloc. Could Germany be making the same mistake again?
NATO membership and EU membership are two very different matters. The EU is a very comprehensive community based on the rule of law. There are 35 negotiating chapters necessary for accession. To rush through the process despite Ukraine not being ready in certain areas would do neither it nor the EU any favors.
At the same time — as the chancellor has also made clear — the idea is not to hold Ukraine back. It has to be clear that once certain milestones are met, the process of European integration will move forward.
Ukraine is fighting to be a European country. That is why I think it goes without saying that Ukraine, too, can be a full member of the European family with free self-determination. We should do everything in our power to support Ukraine on this path.
One issue many in Ukraine are concerned about is corruption and scandals — including those in President Zelenskyy's inner circle. How dangerous are such cases for the international support for Ukraine?
Personally, I am very worried about this. It would be even worse if corruption scandals were not exposed. It is good when corruption cases are thoroughly investigated and there are no false compromises when dealing with them. That is why we will be closely following the verdicts and consequences that result.
I can only encourage Ukrainian civil society, journalists, the public, members of parliament and the opposition to continue keeping a close eye on the situation and to ensure that Ukrainian and European funds are used properly.
Today, there aren't even any serious discussions about peace negotiations with Russia. The Kremlin insists on its maximum demands, which essentially amount to Ukraine's surrender. At the same time, there are forces in Germany, such as the AfD and the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), that have called for talks with Russia. Do you currently envisage any possibilities for diplomatic initiatives?
There have, of course, been numerous attempts by the Ukrainian president and Western states to start peace talks. At the same time, there are no serious signs that the Kremlin has any desire for peace. Such a desire for peace will only emerge when Putin recognizes the futility of his efforts for military conquest.
This requires an increase in military, financial and civil support for Ukraine. And above all, it requires a clear message that the Kremlin cannot hope that Europe will stop supporting Ukraine in 2027 or 2028. We stand with Ukraine — today and tomorrow.
This interview with Johannes Volkmann was conducted by Mykola Berdnyk.

Fungal studies reveal new ways pathogens defeat human immunity
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
16:27:42 CST
17:27:42 KST

MELBOURNE, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- Scientists have discovered how the world's deadliest fungi explode immune cells and shape-shift to defeat the human immune system, providing new avenues for treatments and drug discovery.
Two studies focused on Candida auris and Candida albicans, microscopic fungi that cause life-threatening human infections, opening the door for treatments and antifungal drug discovery by identifying the nutrients the fungi and immune cells use to battle each other, according to a statement released Thursday by Australia's Monash University.
The study published in Nature Communications identified the naturally occurring amino acid alanine that reverses the process these fungi use to defeat the immune system.
When an immune cell swallows a fungal microbe to destroy it, the fungus can trigger a host protein called Ninjurin to form large pores, causing the immune cell to explode and release the fungal cells to spread the infection, researchers said, adding that higher doses of alanine blocked the protein and prevented the immune cells from bursting, thereby containing the fungal cells.
The second study, published in Nature Microbiology, discovered the shape-shifting ability of the mysterious Candida auris, which can adapt itself to stick to human tissue and remain invisible to human immune cells in different parts of the body.
Professor Ana Traven of the Monash Biomedicine Discovery Institute, senior author on both papers, said researchers were looking beyond ways to kill the fungus to explore how the patient's body could be nutritionally manipulated to give the immune system the energy and tools to fight back. ■

====================================================================================================

324-million-year-old insect fossil offers evolutionary link between water, land
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
16:27:40 CST
17:27:40 KST

NANJING, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- An international team led by Chinese researchers has uncovered an early insect species dating back roughly 324 million years that displays both aquatic and terrestrial features, providing direct evidence of how insects gradually made the transition from water to land.
The fossil specimen, named Chosha praecursor, was recovered from Carboniferous strata in the U.S. state of Texas. The work was carried out by scientists from the Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with colleagues from the United Kingdom, the United States, and Spain.
Although the insect already possessed the three pairs of walking legs typical of modern insects, its abdomen retained paddle-shaped lobes suited for swimming. The findings were published online Wednesday in the journal Nature.
Cai Chenyang, a researcher at the institute who led the study, said that abdominal appendages in extant insects are largely reduced, with only the three thoracic pairs remaining. Chosha praecursor, he noted, offers a snapshot of the transition: the ancestral aquatic appendages had not yet disappeared entirely but were being gradually modified and simplified as the insect adapted to life on land.
"This discovery serves as an evolutionary bridge between aquatic and terrestrial life forms," Cai said. "Around 320 million years ago, ancient insects at the water-land interface were progressively evolving new body structures suited to breathing and moving on land."
The fossil, identified as an adult female, measures about 3.2 cm in body length, extending to nearly 5 cm with its elongated tail structure, and has a fusiform shape.
Its thorax bore three pairs of walking legs, and its ovipositor and tail already showed typical insect features. However, segments one through nine of the abdomen still carried segmented appendages, with the rear pairs flattened into paddle-like forms.
Given that the fossil was found in nearshore, shallow-water deltaic deposits, the researchers conclude that Chosha praecursor inhabited humid transitional zones between land and water, retaining clear semi-aquatic characteristics. ■

A high-altitude helicopter has also arrived at the disaster-hit area, the ministry said.
The mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, Xizang, on Wednesday morning. As of 8 a.m. on Thursday, three people had been killed, 558 others remained missing, while two local villagers had been rescued, local authorities said.
Another batch of 111 rescuers from the China Search and Rescue team has arrived at Gyirong County as of 2:28 p.m. Thursday, and will head to Gyirong Port to carry out rescue operations.
An eight-member advance team from China Anneng, a state-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, arrived in Gyirong County early Thursday with communications and detection equipment to collect key data and support efforts to address an upstream blockage, which is a top priority.
Only after the risk posed by the blockage is addressed can the debris accumulated about 3 km upstream of the port be safely cleared, according to rescue personnel at the site.
Hundreds more rescuers, carrying equipment and supplies for detection, rescue, communications and logistical support, are rushing to the site. ■

BEIJING, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said China and the United States should earnestly implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, and remove disruptions and overcome obstacles to high-level exchanges between the two countries, according to a press release issued by China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Thursday.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when meeting with David Perdue, ambassador of the United States to China, on Wednesday in Beijing.
Under the guidance of the two heads of state, both sides are working to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability, Wang noted.
He said facts show that improving bilateral ties, coexisting peacefully on the basis of mutual respect, and achieving win-win cooperation serves the fundamental interests of both peoples and meets the international community's shared expectations.
Both sides should earnestly implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, focus on a constructive agenda, and properly manage differences, he said, calling for efforts to remove disruptions and overcome obstacles to high-level exchanges and push bilateral ties toward stable, healthy and sustainable development.
Both sides are ready to strengthen communication and cooperation to prepare for the next phase of high-level interactions and build a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect and reciprocity, Perdue said.
Perdue expressed condolences on behalf of the U.S. side over the casualties caused by a mudslide that struck a port along the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Wednesday. ■

Drones Attack Ozon Logistics Facilities in Orenburg and Near Ufa

Ukrainian drones attacked two logistics facilities of the Russian marketplace Ozon on August 27 — in Orenburg and near Ufa.
The company’s press service reported this.
According to Ozon, all employees were promptly evacuated from the facilities. Preliminary reports indicate no casualties.
The logistics facility in Orenburg has resumed operations, but FBS shipments will be accepted on a limited basis for one day.
The marketplace said the facility near Ufa, in the Republic of Bashkortostan, sustained minor damage and was temporarily closed for a site inspection.
Most likely, this refers to a warehouse facility located in the city of Blagoveshchensk, about 40 kilometers from the regional capital.
The facility has suspended the acceptance of deliveries from sellers, while shipments in transit are being redirected to other logistics hubs.
The monitoring outlet Exilenova+ published footage showing smoke from a fire near Ufa. It suggested that an Ozon logistics facility may be on fire. At the same time, the Russian company said that customers could place orders as usual.
On August 22, Ukrainian Defense Forces’ drones attacked an Ozon logistics facility in Chapayevsk for the first time, causing fire at the facility.
The following morning, drones struck a warehouse in Orenburg. It became the company’s largest logistics hub in Russia to be attacked, with an area of more than 200,000 square meters.
On the night of August 24, Ukrainian Defense Forces struck three Ozon logistics centers in Dagestan, Stavropol Krai, and Adygea, with a combined area of more than 314,700 square meters.
The largest was the logistics center in the settlement of Tyube, Dagestan, covering about 130,000 square meters. The second-largest was the warehouse in Nevinnomyssk, covering 93,500 square meters, followed by the facility near the settlement of Enem in Adygea, at 91,200 square meters. The strikes sparked large-scale fires at the facilities.

Matildas follow Socceroo footsteps on path to World Cup
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-27
08:21:10 UTC
17:21:10 KST

The Matildas will face South American giants Colombia in two matches ahead of next year's Women's World Cup, with young talent a focus.
Heather Garriock, Football Australia's executive director of football says coach Joe Montemurro will look to emulate Socceroos coach Tony Popovic who gave younger players an opportunity at the men's World Cup this year.
What's next?
The first game against Colombia will be in Canberra on November 28. The date and venue of the second match are yet to be revealed.
The Matildas are looking to follow the Socceroos' blueprint when they play in next year's FIFA Women's World Cup, and two friendlies against Colombia will be a key stepping stone.
On Thursday the Matildas announced they will play the first of two games against the South American giants on November 28 at Canberra Stadium.
The date and venue of the second clash are yet to be determined.
The matches will be an invaluable warm-up ahead of next year's World Cup, which kicks off in Brazil on June 24, with the final on July 25.
Loading Twitter content
And the Matildas, who finished fourth at the 2023 World Cup co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand, are keen to set up the team for long-term success.
With current players including Sam Kerr, Steph Catley, Emily van Egmond and Mackenzie Arnold entering the latter stages of their careers, there are concerns about the Matildas missing such a wealth of talent and experience once they retire.
Heather Garriock, Football Australia's executive director of football, said the friendlies against Colombia would make sure younger players are prioritised.
"We sat down with (coach) Joe (Montemurro) some 12 months ago when he started in the Matildas position, and we asked him what his ideal preparation was in the lead-up to the Women's World Cup," Garriock said on Thursday.
"It was very evident that different styles of play were important to him, but also trying to blood some of the next generation as well.
"We've seen that (younger players getting an opportunity) at the recent World Cup in the US with (Socceroos coach) Tony Popovic as well.
"Joe's style is very creative, very structured and process-driven."
The Socceroos' next generation shone at this year's World Cup in North America, with Nestory Irankunda, Alessandro Circati and Lucas Herrington subsequently earning contracts with major European teams.
The success of the Socceroos' young squad members came after Popovic integrated rising talent into the side in the lead-up to the tournament.
The Matildas are hoping to follow that blueprint, and 21-year-old goalkeeper Chloe Lincoln says getting game time in friendlies against top nations will help her confidence heading into Brazil.
"Playing them (Colombia) at the She Believes Cup, we got a sense of their style, and it's an amazing opportunity to (play) that opposition," Lincoln said.
"Now that the A-League is kicking off again, there's more opportunity for the local players and some of the younger girls playing in that competition to really put … their names forward.
"Especially in these friendly matches, every match really counts, building cohesiveness as a group and working on how we want to perform over in the World Cup."
